title: Add AGENTS.md constitution + Operations Graph V1 (evidence-backed incident memory)
body:
## Goal

1. Give Codex / Claude Code / any other coding agent the same core operating rules, in a
   repository-level constitution rather than a model-specific prompt.
2. Accumulate past production/CI incidents (failure → root cause → fix → regression → PR →
   verification) as verifiable structured data instead of relying on chat history.
3. Let a long-running agent query that history by failure signature, affected file, root-cause
   category, or incident relationship — without depending on a chat log it may never have seen.
4. Never store an agent's own summary as if it were fact: every important claim carries
   GitHub-native evidence (run ID, job ID, commit SHA, PR number, test file), not prose alone.

No engine/prompt/threshold/budget/YouTube behavior changes anywhere in this diff — this PR is
scoped entirely to agent operating infrastructure.

## AGENTS.md rewrite

Restructured into explicit MUST/MUST NOT sections: Authority, Minimal Change, Engine Contracts,
Quality, Budget, Regression, External Provider, Secrets, YouTube, Jev, Landing, Production and
Publishing Boundary, Completion Standard.

**Quality section no longer hardcodes specific threshold numbers.** Evidence for why:
`V3_MAX_API_CALLS`/`V3_MAX_COST_USD`/`ENABLE_HOOK_EXPERIMENT`/`MAX_TOPIC_REGENERATIONS` are not
statically defined anywhere in checked-in source — they're set by workflow env vars and/or
rewritten by `ci_hotfix.py` at CI runtime — and `quality/final_visual_director.py`'s
`semantic_match` floor is domain-conditional (6.0–7.0), not a flat number. A hardcoded "7" here
would already be an oversimplification, and the exact `MAX_TOPIC_REGENERATIONS = 6` literal is
the precise stale value three independent regression assertions carried after production moved
to 19 (see INC-2026-003 below) — direct, current evidence that duplicating a canonical number
into a doc is a real drift risk in this repository, not a hypothetical one. Replaced with
explicit pointers to each value's real canonical source.

**Jev section reflects the actually-reverified current state** (PR #435, draft, not merged to
`main` — confirmed live via `pull_request_read` in this session, not carried forward from any
older summary): strictly a shadow, non-authoritative evaluator, explicitly not a production
invariant.

## Operations Graph V1 (`operations/`)

- `operations/schema.json` — JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for one incident record: run/job IDs,
  commit SHAs, PR numbers, a controlled-vocabulary root-cause category, regression/verification
  evidence, and a limited incident-to-incident relationship vocabulary (`RELATED_TO`,
  `SAME_SIGNATURE_AS`, `REGRESSION_OF`, `SUPERSEDES`).
- `operations/incidents/*.json` — one file per incident, source of truth. No separate
  `index.jsonl` cache — see `operations/README.md` for why a second denormalized index would
  itself be exactly the kind of duplicated-value drift this whole system exists to prevent.
- `operations/query.py` — deterministic local CLI (`--failure-signature`, `--file`,
  `--root-cause`, `--related`, `--list`). No network, no LLM call.
- `operations/validate.py` — schema + evidence-completeness + relationship-integrity validator.
  `VERIFIED` confidence requires all three evidence categories present (failure: run/job id +
  signature; fix: real commit SHA(s); regression+verification: real test files **and** a real
  `PASS`-ing post-fix workflow run) — an incident cannot claim `VERIFIED` by assertion alone, the
  validator checks the actual fields.

### 4 real seed incidents

Each built from evidence re-fetched **live via GitHub tools in this session**, not trusted from
any prior chat/prompt text:

- **INC-2026-001-PEXELS-429** (`PARTIAL`) — the Pexels HTTP 429 crash PR #436 fixes. `PARTIAL`,
  not `VERIFIED`: the original failing run's exact run_id/job_id was not independently re-opened
  this session, only the fix/regression/verification side was — recorded as a real gap, not
  guessed.
- **INC-2026-002-PROVIDER-STATE-TYPEERROR** (`VERIFIED`) — a regression this session found and
  fixed *within* PR #436: a fixture stub `TypeError` silently swallowed by `video_engine.py`'s
  broad `except`, masking a real failure as a "passing" run. Full evidence chain directly
  observed this session.
- **INC-2026-003-MAX-TOPIC-REGEN-DRIFT** (`VERIFIED`) — the exact same stale-assertion pattern
  recurring independently in three files, fixed in PR #430 (30/30 checks green, reconfirmed live
  this session) and ported into PR #436.
- **INC-2026-004-CANDIDATE-BUDGET-EXHAUSTION** (`PARTIAL`) — Candidate Explorer/Gate rewrite-loop
  budget exhaustion from PR #426. Includes an explicit note that the PR's own text mislabeled a
  GitHub-native id as a "job" id when its magnitude actually matches this repo's run-id range —
  corrected here rather than propagated uncritically.

## Tests (`quality/operations_graph_regression_test.py`, 13 cases)

Valid `VERIFIED` incident passes; `VERIFIED` missing verification/fix evidence each fail with a
specific message; duplicate `incident_id` fails; malformed SHA fails; unknown relationship type
fails; dangling relationship fails; `PARTIAL` incident's allowed-missing-field policy enforced
both ways; query by failure signature and by affected file each return the expected incident;
relationship traversal finds both outgoing and incoming edges; `AGENTS.md` exists and contains
its core invariant phrases. All fixtures are synthetic (temp dirs) — independent of the real
seed incidents. No network, no LLM call.

## CI

`.github/workflows/operations_graph_validation.yml` — a new, minimal, dependency-free workflow
(both `operations/validate.py` and `query.py` are pure stdlib) running the validator, the
regression suite, `py_compile`, and a query-CLI smoke test. Never calls OpenAI, Pexels, YouTube,
or generates a video.

## Verified before this PR

- `python operations/validate.py` → PASS (4 incidents)
- `PYTHONPATH=. python quality/operations_graph_regression_test.py` → 13/13 PASS
- `PYTHONPATH=. python -m quality.production_hotfix_chain_structure_regression_test` → PASS
  (confirms this change doesn't disturb the existing hotfix chain SSOT structure)
- `python -m py_compile` on every new/changed Python file
- `yaml.safe_load` on the new workflow file
- `git fetch` + `rev-parse origin/main` re-checked immediately before commit: unchanged at
  `11c151fa80d4fc5ad7e0525cb4c458dafeadfe34`

## Scope explicitly excluded (per instruction)

No engine refactor, no Candidate Explorer algorithm change, no rendering/subtitle/provider
behavior change, no Jev authority change, no model change, no API/cost budget or quality
threshold change, no YouTube upload, no external graph/vector DB, no embedding pipeline.
